Nothing should stand in the way of patients getting the care they need.

This week I urged strong oversight of the use of artificial intelligence by Medicare Advantage companies to protect the health and well-being of Granite Staters.

➡️https://t.co/9xGyDnCm9R https://t.co/n52N3qpI8b

Last month, unlawful robocalls using an AI-generated voice were made to NH voters discouraging them from voting in our presidential primary.

This week I urged @FCC and @FEC to work together to prevent spam robocalls from reaching the American public.

➡️https://t.co/JPQU1bxK4l https://t.co/HTFzB6bBmX
I would certainly agree that VA can and should do more in terms of its use of automation tools, so long as it does not lead to workforce replacement.
Is Jusy an AI chatbot? Maybe put down the device and find out what Granite Staters really think of gutting health care, hungry kids, and $4T more in debt. https://t.co/5HJptmPZHe

I’m also fighting to crack down on AI price gouging.

Big Tech shouldn’t be using your personal information to set tailored prices.

We can’t let algorithms price-gouge working families.
I’m fighting to stop AI price gouging. Big Tech shouldn’t be able to use your personal data to charge you more for groceries.

At Diz’s in Manchester today, folks shared how Trump’s reckless agenda is making it more expensive to put food on the table. 

I’m fighting for changes like eliminating tariffs on groceries and ending AI price-gouging because it shouldn’t be this hard to make ends meet. https://t.co/XsaQU9kWie

Big corporations are raking in record profits while using AI surveillance pricing to raise costs on families who are struggling to put food on the table. It’s outrageous, and Congress needs to step up and put a stop to it immediately.

That’s why I’m introducing the Lower Grocery Prices Act to ban this practice by corporations that jack up food prices and rip off Granite Staters.

Read more: https://t.co/06l7C3YZY6
I’m leading a bill to ban AI price gouging on groceries because companies shouldn’t be allowed to charge you more to feed your family based on your personal data.

Big corporations are using your personal data and AI to charge you more for food, while they rake in record profits.

It’s called surveillance pricing, and here’s how they do it. ⬇️ https://t.co/MZZiGoQkpL

Yeah so this shouldn’t be allowed.

We've got a bill in the House to ban companies from using AI to jack up prices based on your data. Let's get it passed. https://t.co/GgFdZJ101P

You’re not imagining it – the items you need the most are getting more expensive because companies can use AI to track your spending and jack up the price. 

I’m leading a bill to stop that.

At my small business, a cone of ice cream costs the same for everyone. But big corporations are using AI surveillance pricing to jack up costs.

Same price for the same item. That’s how we do it in NH, and it’s not too much to ask. https://t.co/6jVvdkyJy5

The incentives are accelerating AI data center development. And our towns and cities shouldn't have these data centers shoved down their throats without any recourse. They deserve the right to decide what is appropriate for their community.

Data center construction has already increased average electric rates nationwide by up to 6%. In the communities in which they're being built the increases can be even more than that. We know that electricity isn't the only utility affected by data center construction, because it affects water supply and consumption too.

We have to pass meaningful regulation to make sure that AI products are safe, that we're protecting the privacy, the safety, the health of the American public. We have heard deeply concerning reports from people who are involved in the AI space. Designers, technicians, who are coming out and saying that there's potentially a 10% chance that this could obliterate humanity. Who wants to take that chance?

So we can't wait until the genie's out of the bottle. Congress needs to act to set up guardrails that will regulate big tech, that will regulate AI, that builds expertise within the federal government to ensure that there's an approval process before models are made public, that there are minimum safety standards, that we're working on the liability issue, so ultimately, that it's the tech companies that are held accountable when things go wrong, and that we're giving the power to our communities with respect to data center development.

If a proposal comes up for a town, they need to have every opportunity to vet that and reject it. We need to make sure that ratepayers aren't going to be on the hook for massive data center development in New Hampshire or anywhere else.
